hints: Since $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, the perpendicular gradient of $BC$ is $m_{BC} = -\dfrac{1}{-1/2} = 2$.
walkthrough:
The right angle fixes the next side direction before locating the last vertex.
Calculate gradient of side $AB$ and determine the perpendicular gradient of $BC$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 0}{0 - 6} = -\dfrac{3}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$m_{BC} = -\dfrac{1}{-1/2} = 2$$

Set up the gradient formula for $BC$ using $B(0, 3)$ and $C(h, 3h)$:
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{3h - 3}{h - 0} = 2$$
$$3h - 3 = 2h \implies h = 3$$

hints: With $h = 3$, vertex $C$ is $(3, 9)$. Side $CD$ is horizontal, so $y_D = 9$.
Side $AD$ is parallel to $BC$, so $m_{AD} = m_{BC} = 2$.
walkthrough:
The right angle fixes the next side direction before locating the last vertex.
With $h = 3$, $C(h, 3h) = (3, 9)$. Since side $CD$ is parallel to the $x$-axis, the $y$-coordinate of $D$ is constant:
$$y_D = y_C = 9$$
